source: Direct user answers in this conversation; English paraphrases. Prior approvals and clarifications are preserved in ../red-team-integration-2026-10-14/README.md.

questions.title: Privacy monetisation
questions.response_summary: Eve's main advantage is fewer vacancies; the user considers tenant demand sufficient.
questions.analyst_disposition: Prioritise void duration/replacement evidence, without booking higher rent or occupancy.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Matched ordinary leases, actual vacancy/renewal and rival package explanations.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Local whole-unit substitutes
questions.response_summary: Eve offers compact single-person privacy, easier cleaning and a higher-end project experience; Pacific Place is perceived as more budget/room-rental oriented. Later clarification replaces lower fees with less upward fee pressure.
questions.analyst_disposition: Separate user-attributed positioning from a resident census and verified charges.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Actual target cohort, whole-unit substitutes, repair load, fee history, funding and service outcomes.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Young compact owner buyers
questions.response_summary: Established community amenities and local roots may attract young compact owner buyers; temporary school-led tenants are less likely to buy locally.
questions.analyst_disposition: Local attachment is a candidate buyer route, not proven housing-form adoption.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Actual funded compact buyers, motives, budgets, alternatives and ownership willingness.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Pines rental families versus purchasing families
questions.response_summary: Pines, and user-nominated Palma/Pelangi comparators, appeal to local and foreign families through community and management. The user later agrees that demand does not ensure the next buyer pays more, while retaining a price-support view.
questions.analyst_disposition: Retain family-adoption hypothesis; no guaranteed price floor. Palma/Pelangi are leads, not admitted new cases.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Family buying versus renting, supported exit quantum, current governance/works and substitutes.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Zeva price premium versus saleability
questions.response_summary: Zeva should sell more easily than Solstice because of amenities and a more varied community, but the user does not expect a higher price or necessarily appreciation, citing Seri Kembangan stigma.
questions.analyst_disposition: Saleability hypothesis only; no premium or yield compression.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Buyer depth, time/discount to sale, captured demand diversity, funded investor exits.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Useful rooms, bays and household duration
questions.response_summary: Two usable bays can outweigh an extra bedroom or space for city couples/families. The user confirms this is contextual, not universal.
questions.analyst_disposition: Apply the approved two-vehicle household scope; preserve compact/investor eligibility.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Legal/practical bays, additional cost, actual household vehicles and relevant alternatives.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Where landed substitution actually binds
questions.response_summary: Older landed security/ageing may favour condos; newer planned gated/guarded landed may attract outer-area buyers. The user retains older-landed stagnation as a view.
questions.analyst_disposition: Keep attributed stagnation hypothesis and matched landed alternatives; no permanent price law.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Matched condition, security, total budget, routes and actual older-landed prices/demand.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Older affordability versus newer product
questions.response_summary: Resident behaviour and management effectiveness are the user's two key project-level factors after initial product screening, particularly 5-10 years after completion.
questions.analyst_disposition: Separate project appreciation from individual return; retain other Core mechanisms and re-open missed/changed physical issues when needed.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Operating behaviour, management ability/funding/results, matched price trajectory and counterexamples.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Prime owner utility and income weakness
questions.response_summary: Much prime-area utility is already priced in; owner-use or trophy demand does not ensure attractive investment terms.
questions.analyst_disposition: Keep utility and acquisition economics separate.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Matched buyer willingness and price/return evidence; no automatic prestige premium.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Who pays for central employment-node housing
questions.response_summary: Third-party-funded foreign executives/students may support premium rents more readily than self-paying tenants. The user approves separate resident/payer/budget checks.
questions.analyst_disposition: Payer and budget structure matter; nationality alone does not establish capacity or willingness.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Payment limits, lease duration, employer/provider alternatives and actual node-specific capture.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Different prime family catchments
questions.response_summary: School choice is usually the main boundary for family catchments.
questions.analyst_disposition: Use specific school and daily routines rather than one pooled international-family market.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: School/route substitution, household budgets and project-level capture.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Student and institutional accommodation segmentation
questions.response_summary: Initial view distinguishes wealthier private-university whole-unit demand from budget-limited local-university demand. The user subsequently approves payer, institution-rule and accommodation-alternative checks.
questions.analyst_disposition: Do not operationalise the initial statement as a universal segmentation rule.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Institution/year-specific rules, budgets, freedom to live off-campus and provider competition.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Hospital access and ordinary lease duration
questions.response_summary: Short-stay hospital demand is distinct; longer-term demand chiefly comes from regular employees and shift workers.
questions.analyst_disposition: Do not use transient demand to support ordinary annual tenancy.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Actual staff leases, schedules, access and tenant mix.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Puchong's internal market boundaries
questions.response_summary: Commercial-centre proximity is associated in the user's judgment with higher prices, convenience and upscale appeal; the user accepts separating benefits and price.
questions.analyst_disposition: Test convenience and nuisances independently; high price does not prove quality.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Matched household substitution, paid rent, total budget and negative externalities.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Western employment growth and private tenants
questions.response_summary: Western industrial workers often prefer rooms; family tenants may choose landed for more space and lower rent, depending on industry.
questions.analyst_disposition: Treat employment-to-private-condo capture as conditional.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Actual industry/cohort, employer housing, room/landed alternatives and budgets.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Airport corridor housing budgets
questions.response_summary: Cabin crew are the proposed airport-corridor cohort seeking better condo environments without excessive distance.
questions.analyst_disposition: Specific target cohort to investigate; no automatic allocation of airport workers.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Shift-compatible door-to-door access, budget/payer, leases and alternatives.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: New-township high-rise adoption
questions.response_summary: Township demand is staged: early spillover from older/expensive districts, then later arrivals for employment/schools as the township matures.
questions.analyst_disposition: Do not assume inevitable apartment maturity or double-count movers.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Household origins/timing, jobs, housing-form adoption and retained demand.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Competitive supply versus complementary supply
questions.response_summary: Different lifestyles may reduce direct competition; the user accepts stage and effective-substitution refinements.
questions.analyst_disposition: No blanket exemption from competing supply; test indirect budget/upgrade substitution.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Actual competing layouts, packages, incentives, delivery and tenant choices.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Cheap outliers and recovery from stigma
questions.response_summary: The user states the SqWhere distress/auction/stigma case was verified by them and accepts that cheap auction purchases need not exit at the desired price.
questions.analyst_disposition: Record user-verified provenance, not independent analyst verification; retain stigma-recovery and exit checks.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Effective basis, liabilities, continuing supply, catalyst transmission and financeable resales.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Durable furnishing and refurbishment value
questions.response_summary: Tenant-specific function should guide improvements; internet/desks may matter more to students, and fixed improvements are favoured. The user approves separate recovery/lifecycle tests.
questions.analyst_disposition: No universal fixed-versus-movable recovery rule.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Incremental cost, useful life, paid rent/retention, replacement and supported resale recovery.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Hidden exit ceilings and ageing
questions.response_summary: Mixed circulation and noise are key risks; resident behaviour and management repair efficiency matter. Scope is later clarified to post-screening project stewardship.
questions.analyst_disposition: Operational and inherent-design risks remain separate.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Observed use/noise, circulation/lift capacity, management funding and buyer penalties.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Specific transition exceptions and their deadline
questions.response_summary: Kwasa is the user's strongest transition candidate. The user attributes present rental demand to nearby established employment areas including Kota Damansara, Mutiara Damansara and Bandar Utama, and expects later high-end offices within Kwasa to add demand. Other new townships are expected to mature more slowly without comparable nearby support.
questions.analyst_disposition: Kwasa leads hypothesis validation within the named township/transition group only. No verified tenant mix, office pipeline, rent growth, delivery date or investment clearance is asserted.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Verify existing spillover, actual office occupation and jobs, incremental versus relocated demand, selected residential capture, supply and funded delay. Establish a finite evidence-based review/deadline before an actionable transition case; no date supplied by user.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Cross-area concentration overlooked by labels
questions.response_summary: Bandar Puteri and TRX are distinguished by surrounding mature amenities. The remaining candidates depend on similar buyer/tenant sources. The user explicitly clarifies that remaining means the named township candidates, not all projects such as Eve/Pines.
questions.analyst_disposition: Scope common spillover/employment-maturation exposure to Kwasa, Elmina/Denai Alam, Gamuda Gardens and the western-township candidates. This does not imply identical tenants, perfect correlation or zero risk for the exceptions.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Map actual origins, employers, budgets and competing supply; no numeric correlations or changed stress results.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

questions.title: Challenge the overall evidence queue
questions.response_summary: No additional challenge to the current research preferences.
questions.analyst_disposition: Record no further ranking objection; this is not endorsement of every assumption, a buy instruction or execution-start approval.
questions.remaining_analyst_evidence_work: Existing case-specific empirical holds persist.
questions.status: Response received; interpretation recorded; empirical claims not certified

analyst_review_status: Ready for explicit user closure/start confirmation
